item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves Add behavior, and keeps scope focused. A introduces explicitly forbidden APIs and retry refactoring.","reasons":["B declares the required API exactly: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead accepts ...UploadFileOption, breaking the specified API contract.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile directly. A creates NewFileWithFields and builds new multipart-field machinery despite the explicit reuse requirement.","A adds association fields and several public option types/functions, directly contradicting the instruction not to add association fields or change FilesOption behavior.","A changes generic request/retry behavior for seekable readers and changes Add semantics, despite the contract requiring unrelated retry machinery and Add behavior to remain unchanged. B leaves that machinery alone and documents Add's existing limitation accurately enough for its implementation context."],"risks_a":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request/response logic.","The new seek-based GetBody closes over one shared reader and is unsafe if request-body recreation overlaps; it also materially changes body ownership semantics.","Tests still do not visibly cover Upload source-reader failure propagation."],"risks_b":["Upload incorrectly calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing the encoded body through FilesService.Add, duplicating option handling, request construction, response decoding, and errors.","The added tests do not visibly cover empty-filename validation, nil-content validation, source-reader failures, or FilesOption propagation through Upload.","Documentation says Upload handles a local file even though the API accepts any io.Reader; this is unnecessarily narrow wording."]}
